{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01TG9aDVzKVred1EW15RqApo","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t[![build-openlane-sky130](https://github.com/secworks/aes/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg?branch=master&event=push)](https://github.com/secworks/aes/actions/workflows/ci.yml)\n2\t\n3\taes\n4\t===\n5\t\n6\tVerilog implementation of the [symmetric block cipher AES (NIST FIPS 197)](http://csrc.nist.gov/publications/fips/fips197/fips-197.pdf).\n7\t\n8\t\n9\t## Status ##\n10\tThe core is completed, has been used in several FPGA and ASIC\n11\tdesigns. The core is well tested and mature.\n12\t\n13\t\n14\t## Introduction ##\n15\t\n16\tThis implementation supports 128 and 256 bit keys. The\n17\timplementation is iterative and process one 128 block at a time. Blocks\n18\tare processed on a word level with 4 S-boxes in the data path. The\n19\tS-boxes for encryption are shared with the key expansion and the core\n20\tcan thus not do key update in parallel with block processing.\n21\t\n22\tThe encipher and decipher block processing datapaths are separated and\n23\tbasically self contained given access to a set of round keys and a\n24\tblock. This makes it possible to hard wire the core to only encipher or\n25\tdecipher operation. This allows the synthesis/build tools to optimize\n26\taway the other functionality which will reduce the size to about\n27\t50%. This has been tested to verify that decryption is removed and the\n28\tcore still works.\n29\t\n30\tFor cipher modes such as CTR, CCM, CMAC, GCM the decryption\n31\tfunctionality in the AES core will never be used and thus the decipher\n32\tblock processing can be removed.\n33\t\n34\tThis is a fairly compact implementation. Further reduction could be\n35\tachived by just having a single S-box. Similarly the performane can be\n36\tincreased by having 8 or even 16 S-boxes which would reduce the number\n37\tof cycles to two cycles for each round.\n38\t\n39\t\n40\t### Contact information ##\n41\t\n42\tAssured provides customer support including customization, integration\n43\tand system development related to the core. For more information,\n44\tplease contact [Assured Security\n45\tConsultants](https://www.assured.se/contact).\n46\t\n47\t\n48\t## Branches ##\n49\t\n50\tThere are several branches available that provides different versions of\n51\tthe core. The branches are not planned to be merged into master. The\n52\tbranches available that provides versions of the core are:\n53\t\n54\t\n55\t### on-the-fly-keygen ###\n56\t\n57\tThis version of AES implements the key expansion using an on-the-fly\n58\tmechanism. This allows the initial key expansion to be removed. This\n59\tsaves a number of cycles and also remove almost 1800 registers needed to\n60\tstore the round keys. Note that this version of AES only supports\n61\tencryption. On-the-fly key generation does not work with\n62\tdecryption. Decryption must be handled by the block cipher mode - for\n63\texample CTR.\n64\t\n65\t\n66\t### dual-keys ###\n67\t\n68\tThis version of AES supports two separate banks of expanded keys to\n69\tallow fast key switching between two keys. This is useful for example in\n70\tan AEAD mode with CBC + CMAC implemented using a single AES core.\n71\t\n72\t\n73\t### cmt-sbox ###\n74\t\n75\tAn experimental version of the core in which the S-box is implemented\n76\tusing circuit minimized logic functions of a ROM table. The specific\n77\ttable used is\n78\t[the 113 gate circuit](http://cs-www.cs.yale.edu/homes/peralta/CircuitStuff/SLP_AES_113.txt) by the [CMT team at Yale](http://cs-www.cs.yale.edu/homes/peralta/CircuitStuff/CMT.html).\n79\t\n80\tSome area and performance results using the cmt_sbox compared to\n81\tmaster:\n82\t\n83\t#### Altera\n84\t- Tool: Quartus Prime 19.1.0\n85\t- Device: Cyclone V (5CGXFC7C7F23C8)\n86\t- master (S-box implemented with a table)\n87\t  - ALMs: 2599\n88\t  - Regs: 3184\n89\t  - Fmax: 93 MHz\n90\t  - aes_sbox: 160 ALUTs\n91\t\n92\t- cmt_sbox\n93\t  - ALMs: 2759\n94\t  - Regs: 3147\n95\t  - Fmax: 69 MHz\n96\t  - aes_sbox: 363 ALUTs\n97\t\n98\t\n99\t#### Xilinx\n100\t- Tool: Vivado 2019.2\n101\t- Device: Kintex-7 (7k70tfbv676-1)\n102\t- master:\n103\t  - LUTs: 3020\n104\t  - FFs: 2992\n105\t  - Fmax: 125 MHz\n106\t\n107\t- cmt_sbox:\n108\t  - LUTs: 2955\n109\t  - FFs: 2992\n110\t  - Fmax: 105 MHz\n111\t\n112\t\n113\t## Core Usage\n114\t\n115\t### Usage sequence:\n116\t1. Load the key to be used by writing to the key register words.\n117\t2. Set the key length by writing to the config register.\n118\t3. Initialize key expansion by writing a one to the init bit in the control register.\n119\t4. Wait for the ready bit in the status register to be cleared and then to be set again. This means that the key expansion has been completed.\n120\t5. Write the cleartext block to the block registers.\n121\t6. Start block processing by writing a one to the next bit in the control register.\n122\t7. Wait for the ready bit in the status register to be cleared and then to be set again.
